newsitem.title: UK: EFT gains after Bank of Scotland bid.
newsitem.headline: EFT gains after Bank of Scotland bid.

text.p: Shares in leasing group EFT Group Plc rose in early trade on Tuesday, responding to an agreed bid from Bank of Scotland Plc announced after the London market's close on Monday.
EFT shares were up 36p at 170-1/2 by 0748 GMT in volume of 10,000 shares.

Under the offer, EFT shareholders will receive 175p in cash for each of their shares, representing a premium of 30.1 percent over their mid-market price at the close of business on 27 June and valuing EFT Group at 89.6 million stg.
Bank of Scotland said it intended to integrate EFT and its British Linen Leasing unit in a single division within its British Linen Bank operation.
"The acquisition of EFT Group is in line with our strategy of developing profitable niche businesses," said Peter Burt, Bank of Scotland chief executive.
"It will help us to grow further the scale and quality of our asset finance and leasing activities and to fulfil the combined potential of both companies."
EFT chairman Hamish Grossart said the group could better capitalise on growth opportunities as part of a larger group.
"In the board's view, the Bank of Scotland offer represents attractive value to our shareholders and enhances the opportunities for EFT Group," Grossart said.
